newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - July 30.
newsitem.headline: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - July 30.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:
The Reserve Bank of Australia cut official interest rates by 0.5 percentage points to 5.0 percent.

Canada's Barrick Gold Corp is expected to launch a A$3.40 per share cash takeover bid for Australian gold miner Great Central Mines Ltd, The Australian newspaper reported on Wednesday. Also foreign exchange dealers reported a large buy order for AUD/CAD worth around A$450 million from a Canadian corporate which was rumoured to be linked to the takeover of an Australian mining company.

Interactive Flight Technologies Inc said Tuesday that Qantas Airways has decided not to install a new interactive in-flight entertainment system for its long haul fleet. Instead, Qantas decided to keep its existing in-flight system for the time being, Interactive Flight said.

Grocery wholesaler and retailer Davids Ltd is expected to announce senior management changes, the sale of some non-retail assets and possible asset writedowns on Wednesday, The Australian Financial Review newspaper said.
* Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd A$18.22 (-0.11)

The British government may prosecute Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd over the leak of a polluting substance earlier this month from an oil and gas rig off Britain's coast, Environment Minister Michael Meacher said on Tuesday.

Gold miner Plutonic Resources Ltd said on Tuesday its gold production rose to a record 138,231 ounces in the quarter ended June 30 from 121,922 in the March quarter, while cash operating costs fell sharply.

However, the poor performance of the gold market and a decline in hedging prospects had led the company to review its operations, while orebody development has been suspended at its Mt Morgans mine, Plutonic said in its quarterly report.
